deep.reconstruction:
The page has no derivation, formula or computation. It is a stencil sheet and a periodic number pattern on squared paper.

(a) Heading 'Fenster' (window) and folio number 48 (circled).

(b) The window. A square frame about 9x9 grid cells encloses a black square about 8x8 cells. It is most probably not ink: the uniformly black field matches the black background around the leaf, so it is likely a hole cut in the paper. That would make the sheet a mask to lay over another sheet. This is my inference.

(c) The pattern below. Number grid columns from the left margin cell (c=0) and rows from the first number row (r=0). Two 2x3 blocks of digits occur, mirror images of each other:
- A = [[7,4],[5,3],[1,6]].
- B = [[4,7],[3,5],[6,1]], i.e. A with its columns swapped.
- Single 2s stand between them.

Positions as read from the image (my coordinate reading):
- '2' at (r,c) = (0,8), (4,0), (4,8) [boxed], (8,0), (8,8), (12,8).
- A occupies rows 1-3 and 9-11, columns 1-2 and 9-10.
- B occupies rows 5-7 and 13-15, columns 6-7 and 14-15.

So the arrangement is doubly periodic with period 8 horizontally and vertically: A at (r,c) ≡ (1..3, 1..2) mod 8, B at (5..7, 6..7) mod 8, and 2 at c ≡ 0 mod 8 with r ≡ 0 mod 4. The 2s at column 0 for rows 0 and 12 are simply not written.

The period 8 equals the side of the window, about 8 cells. Wherever an 8x8 window is placed (aligned to the grid), it shows exactly one fundamental domain of the pattern: 14 numbered cells, each label 1-7 appearing exactly twice. The boxed 2 may mark a reference or origin position for placing the window.

The purpose cannot be fixed from this page alone; there are no neighbouring pages. Possibilities include a reading mask for a table, an ornament or tiling design, or a scheme for seven labels such as weekdays. The labels 1-7 with 2 kept separate are suggestive but not decisive.

No mathematical derivation is present.

results.what: Doubly periodic (period 8x8) placement of the labels 1-7 on the square lattice, built from a 2x3 block and its mirror image, with an 8x8 window/mask sized to one period
results.modern_name: periodic lattice pattern / fundamental domain of a wallpaper-type arrangement; reading mask (stencil)
results.usually_credited_to: no specific attribution (routine combinatorial or ornamental construction)

deep.surprise_reason: The sheet contains only a window/mask drawing and a simple periodic arrangement of digits, with no theorem or derivation. Its purpose is unclear but nothing on it is mathematically non-trivial.

checkable.asserts: Block B is block A with its two columns swapped (a mirror image)
Block A together with the separate 2 uses each of the labels 1..7 exactly once
One 8x8 period contains 14 labelled cells (A, B and two 2s), so each of the 7 labels appears exactly twice per window-sized period
Horizontal offsets between repeated blocks (A: col 1 to 9; B: col 6 to 14; 2: col 0 to 8) are multiples of 8, i.e. horizontal period 8

transcription_corrections: The black square is very probably a hole cut in the leaf (the black background showing through), not an inked drawing; the sheet is a stencil or mask ('Fenster').

The positions of the blocks matter and the linear transcription loses them. The left-hand 7/4 blocks are in columns 1-2 and the next 7/4 blocks in columns 9-10. The 4/7 blocks are in columns 6-7 and 14-15. The 2s in the middle column are at column 8; the small 2s at the far left margin (column 0) occur only in rows 4 and 8.
The dot in '7. 4' (first row) is a stray mark, not a decimal point; there are also stray dots elsewhere (e.g. left of the second 4/7 block, at the right edge).
